Bureau, Deputy Director (Law), Group ‘A’ Post, Recruitment Rules, 2026.

other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.- No person,- 


(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse 
living; or 

(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any 
person, 


shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, 
relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons.

G.S.R. 97.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution and in

in the Union Public Service Commission, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Union Public Service Commission, 
Assistant Director (Confidential), Group ‘A’ Post, Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in the pay matrix. - The number of post, its classification and

(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to any of the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
such person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. — Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, 
it may, by order, and for reasons to be recorded in writing, and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect of any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Ex-servicemen, the Other Backward Classes 
and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to 
time in this regard.

supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of the 
Superintendent in Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, namely: 


1. Short title and commencement.- (1) These rules may be called the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal Superintendent 
(Group ‘B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2026.

2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said post, its classification and level

and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule.

(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 


(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person,

AWARD 


By order NO.L-202/83/20l7 (IR(B-ID): Dated: 6/0I/20l8, the present industrial dispute has been 
referred for adjudication in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub-section (2A) of 
Section l0 the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947) by the Central Government, with following schedule: 


"Whether the action of the Management of Chief Manager/Circle Head, Punjab National Bank, Divisional 
Office, Faizabad and Zonal Manager, Faizabad in termination of Shri Sabind Kumar, s/o Late Shri 
Rambhajan from 92/04/20/7 alleged to be working from /5///2075 in PNB, Rojagaonjs Legal and justified 
? If not, what relief he is entitled to?" 


[भाग [खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 2, 2026/वैशाख 2, 948 4007 
Accordingly, an I.D. Case No. /208 has been registered. 
In response to which claimant, filed his statement of claim. 


In brief facts as stated therein are that he was appointed as casual labour with the respondent on 08..205, and 
worked up till 07.04.207, however his services were retrenched/terminated without complying provisions of Section 
25F of the Industrial Dispute Act. 


Accordingly it is prayed by claimant, that he may be reinstated back in his services. 


Thereafter on behalf of respondent, written statement has been filed denying the contention as taken by claimant in 
his claim petition to which respondent had filed rejoinder affidavit. 


On 22.04.20I9 on behalf of claimant document no. (W6-l) to (W6-3l), were filed in support of his case, and on 
behalf of respondent/Bank documents no.(M7-) to (M7-4) were filed on 7.02.2020, on record. 


Thereafter on 24.2.2020, claimant in order to support his case has filed evidence on affidavit (examination in 
chief)(W-8). 


From the perusal of record its transpired that in spite of repeated opportunity given to applicant, he does not turn up 
for his cross examination on the evidence in chief filed by him, so by order dated 0.09.2024, right of workman to 
cross examine himself on his evidence on affidavit (Examination in Chief) has been closed. 


Thereafter the matter was listed for hearing, in spite of notice none appeared on behalf of workman. 


Today (05.02.2026) the matter was taken up in the revise cause list neither workman nor any counsel/LR appear on 
behalf of the workman, in spite of notice. 


Shri AP Singh learned counsel for respondent is present. 


I have heard Shri AP Singh learned counsel for respondent and perused the record, keeping in view the above said 
facts, this is a case of no evidence because worker did not cross examined himself on the evidence filed by him on 
affidavit (examination in chief) so the case as set up by him has not been proved as per the relevant provision 
Evidence Act, keeping the said facts and the law as laid by the Hon'ble High Court in the case of V. K. Raj 
Industries v. Labour Court (l) and others 98 (29) FLR 94 as under: 


"It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove 
illegality of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail 
Whenever a workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative 
for him to file written statement before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is 
challenged and he must also produce evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file 
written statement or produce evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered in 
favour of the workman and he would not be entitled to any relief." 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding 
Officer, Labour Court (II), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (8) FLR 64 Hon'ble Allahabad High Court has held 
as under: 


"The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., 
V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. /964 (49) 
FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. /996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led 
by or on behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In 
such a situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead 
evidence to establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, 
who would fail if no evidence is led." 


And by the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 
Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co- operative Bank Ltd. 200 (26) FLR 59; wherein it has been held 
as under: 


"The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the shoulders of the 
respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead evidence first which he failed. 
A perusal of the impugned award also does not show that any evidence either oral or documentary was led 
by the respondent. In the case of no evidence, the reference has to be dismissed." 


AWARD 
For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief. 
Award as above.

“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., 
V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. /964 (49) 
FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. /996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led 
by or on behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In 
such a situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead 
evidence to establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, 
who would fail if no evidence is led.” 


And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 
Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2070 (726) FLR 5I9; wherein it has been held as 
under: 


“The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the 
shoulders of the respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead 
evidence first which he failed. A perusal of the impugned award also does not show that any evidence 
either oral or documentary was led by the respondent. In the case of no evidence, the reference has 
to be dismissed.” 


As the workman did not file any evidence on affidavit in support of his case, so it is a case of no evidence filed on 
behalf of workman in support of case, liable to be dismissed. 


For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief. 
Award as above.

2. The schedule mentioned in that order is: 


“Whether the demand of Shri R.Elangovan, Sub-Staff of Andhra Bank for reinstatement into service w.e.f 
97.//.2048 (Stated to be working since 93.72.2074॥0 0/.77.2076) with all attendant benefits is legal and justified? 
If not, to what reliefis the workman entitled to?” 


3. It is the claim of the Petitioner that he was selected and appointed by the Respondent Management as sub- 
staff, after having followed the existent instructions and procedures, in the Sriperumbudur Branch (Tiruvallur District) 
on 03.2.20I4. The petitioner submits that he had worked for more than 240 days in each of the calendar years during 
the period from December 20!4 to October, 208. The petitioner further submits that his monthly wages was 
deposited in his bank a/c bearing no. 24l!000002698 at Sriperumbudur Branch of the Respondent bank. The 
petitioner submits that his last drawn salary of Rs.!5,082/- being the salary for the month of June 208 was deposited 
in his bank account on 03.07.20l8. The petitioner submits that he had put in total service of more than 4 years from 
the date of appointment i.e. 03.2.204, till the date of termination i.e. 3.0.20l8. The action of the respondent in 
terminating the services of the petitioner during the pendency of conciliation proceedings is arbitrary, vindictive, 
illegal and against the principles of natural justice. The respondent bank violated the provisions of the Industrial 
Disputes Act, 947, arbitrarily in terminating him from service without complying with the provisions of the Act. 
The petitioner submits that it is pertinent to mention that even when he was terminated from service without notice, 
the Respondent has issued online advertisement during April, 207 calling for applications for the post of sub staff 
without filling from amongst the existing staff working for years together. The provisions of the bi-partite settlement 
with regard to the regularization of temporary staff have also been totally violated in terminating the services of the 
petitioner. For the above reasons, the Respondent Bank may be directed to reinstate the Petitioner into service with 
back wages, continuity of service and other attendant benefits. 


4. The Respondent bank in its counter statement submitted that the Petitioner was never appointed at the said 
branch of the bank as a sub-staff. He was engaged for specific purpose for which he was paid with fair wages on 
the basis of equal pay for equal work. Therefore, his engagement was casual in nature and it shall not amount to 
appointment in the post of sub-staff. Hence, the services provided by the Petitioner was no stretch of imagination 
can be considered as regularization. It is submitted that disengagement of Petitioner during pendency of conciliation 
is not arbitrary, illegal and against the principles of natural justice. The Petitioner was not appointed as sub-staff, 
whereas he was just engaged for completion of specific purpose. The Petitioner was never terminated from service 
and thus, no notice was served on the Petitioner and there is no violation of law committed by the Respondent bank 
and thus, for the above reasons, the ID raised by the Petitioner is not maintainable and deserves to be dismissed.

5. Heard both the counsels appearing on behalf of the parties and perused the records. The Petitioner has filed 
proof of affidavit and six documents have been marked as Ex.WI to W6 on his behalf and the Petitioner was cross 
examined by the Respondent. On behalf of the Respondent proof of affidavit was filed by the Chief Manager of 
Zonal Office Mr. K.Satyanarayana. No document is filed on behalf of the Respondent bank. 


6. The point that arises for determination is whether the Petitioner is entitled for reinstatement into service? 
If so, to what relief, he is entitled to? 


7. The learned counsel for the Appellant submitted that the Petitioner was appointed by the Respondent Bank after 
having followed the existent instructions on 03.2.20I4 and he has completed four years service without any break. 
The monthly wages of the Petitioner was credited into account of the Petitioner in Sriperumbudur branch bearing 
No.24!000002698. In this regard, the Petitioner has marked Ex.WI] as transaction history, which clearly 
establishes the fact that Petitioner had continuously worked with the Respondent bank for four years i.e., more 
than 240 days in a calendar year and wages were drawn. Ex.W2 and Ex.W3 are the letters sent by Branch Manager of 
Sriperumbudur branch of the Respondent bank to the DGM., Zonal Office recommending the Petitioner for 
confirmation. 


8. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Respondent contended that the engagement of the Petitioner was 
casual in nature and shall not amount to appointment for the post of sub-staff. Merely because the Petitioner has 
completed 240 days of service in a year preceding the date of disengagement, the service of the Petitioner is not 
liable to be regularized. He further submitted that when there is no order of appointment, the question of termination 
of the Petitioner does not arise. Further, in the proof of affidavit, the Respondent stated that the Petitioner had raised 
conciliation proceedings during the year 208 u/s.2A of the Act. Therefore, the present industrial dispute raised by 
the Petitioner attracts doctrine of res judicata as the Petitioner has raised similar dispute before this forum through 
union and the matter was earlier dismissed by this Tribunal. Therefore, it is second round of litigation. On this 
ground itself, the ID is liable to be dismissed and the question of adjudication of this dispute does not arise. 


9. The learned Counsel for the Respondent relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case 
of Secretary, State of Karnataka Vs. Umadevi & Others in Appeal (Civil) 3595-362 of 999 (2006) 4 SCC I. In 
this case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.3595-362 of 999, 3520-3524 of 2002 arising out of SLP 
903-905 of 200l dated 0.04.2006 has directed the Union of India, that long and continuous service alone does 
not create right to regularization. It cannot be claimed as a matter of right, unless appointment itself is made against 
the sanctioned post and it was made through legal and proper process. 


0. The Respondent further contended that no person can be appointed in violation of recruitment norms laid 
down. Any appointment is made in violation of recruitment norms, the said appointment becomes void ab-initio and it 
does not confer any right to the persons so appointed. 


ll. The learned counsel for the Respondent relied upon the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in The 
Managing Director Vs. Ajmer Vidhyut Vitran Nigam Ltd & Another. In that case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has 
held that the date from which the regularization is to be granted is a matter to be decided by the employer keeping in 
view a number of factors like nature of work, number of posts lying vacant, financial condition of the employer, the 
additional financial burden caused, suitability of the workman for the job and the manner and reason for which 
initial appointments were made etc. and further held that date of regularization and grant of pay scale is a prerogative 
of the employer / screening committee and no parity can be claimed in the matter of regularization in different years. 


[भाग ॥-.ख एण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 2, 2026/वैशाख 2, 948 407 


I23 The learned counsel for the Respondent relied upon another judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, The 
State of Bihar and Ors Vs. Kirti Narayan Prasad. In that case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that since the 
appointment of the Petitioner was ab initio, void, they cannot be said to be civil servants of the State. On perusal of 
the judgement, it appears that some Petitioners produced fake or forged appointment letter. But, this is not the case of 
the Petitioner. He never forged the appointment letter. Further, the Respondent failed to refute the documentary 
evidence ४5.9७] filed by the Petitioner that the wages amount was paid to the Petitioner for all these four years. 


3. As held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is the prerogative right of the employer to regularize the services 
of employee But, if the employee serves continuously for four years, then he cannot be asked to leave the service 
without providing opportunity of being heard. Therefore, in the present case, the Petitioner is entitled for 
reinstatement into service. 


AWARD 


In view of the above reasons, the Industrial Dispute raised by Petitioner is allowed. The Respondent is directed to 
reinstate the Petitioner on the same pay scale as he was getting from the date of removal. The Petitioner is entitled 
for 50% of the back wages, which will be paid within three months and also entitled for regularization in the course 
of seniority as per availability of regular post. The reference is answered accordingly.

The Central Government, Ministry of Labour & Employment vide its Order No.L-!20/08/20I7(IR(B-II) 
dated 20-03-207 referred the following Industrial Dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication: - 


2. The schedule mentioned in that order is: 


“Whether the action of the management of Indian Overseas Bank , Regional Office, Madurai in estopping 
the services of Shri S.Jeyaramalingam, an Ex-Jewel Appraiser from service w.e.f ०6.03,.2075 is legal and 
justified? If not, to what relief, the workman is entitled to?” 


3 As per the claim statement, the case of the Petitioner is that he was engaged as Business Correspondent to 
the bank as per agreement dated .08.20l0 and later he was appointed as jewel appraiser from 05.!0.20I2 for 
Sevalpatti Branch. The Petitioner was terminated by the bank without adopting any procedure and he was not 
assigned any reason for termination. The Petitioner submits that reported allegation of undervalue of gold jewels 
against him had not been established. There is no substantial evidence to prove the allegation was made against the 
Petitioner. No show cause notice has been issued and termination of service is against provisions of Article [4, 6 & 
2 of Constitution of India. Therefore, the Respondent bank may be directed to reinstate the petitioner into service . 


4. In the counter statement filed on behalf of the Respondent, it is submitted that the petitioner has raised the 
present industrial dispute challenging his dis-empanelment as jewel appraiser under Industrial Disputes Act 947, is 
not maintainable either in law or on facts and it is liable to be dismissed in limine, as jewel appraisers are not 
workmen as defined under Section 2(S) of the same Act. That the jewel appraisers are not workmen is amply clear 
from the rulings dated !0.03.2006 of the Honourable Supreme Court in the Appeal (civil) 7986 of 2004 in Writ 
Appeal No.465 of 200] in the case of the General Manager, Indian Overseas Bank - vs - Workmen, All India 
Overseas Bank Employees Union. In as much as the jewel appraisers are not workmen, the dispute raised by them 
against Indian Overseas Bank is not an Industrial Dispute in terms of provision of the Industrial Disputes Act. 


5. In fact as per policy Bank never appoints any jewel appraiser. As per guidelines of the Bank, a panel of jewel 
appraisers will be prepared based on the applications made by experienced jewel appraisers and among the 
empanelled appraisers, the branch can utilize the service of any one of them with the approval of the Regional Office. 
Since the Bank has not appointed the petitioner on employment basis, they are free to carry on any business even 
while certifying the jewels at the opposite party Bank. The bank has chosen to disengage the petitioner since he has 
given certificate to inferior quality jewels and also due to other allegations. It is submitted that there is no employer 
and employee relationship between the Bank and the petitioner. The petitioner was empaneled in the Jewel Appraiser 
panel and allotted to the Sevalpatti Branch on 05.0.20l2. His service as jewel appraiser was dispensed with by 
Regional office Madurai based on complaints against him by the customers of the Bank. Regional office of the Bank 
conducted re-appraisal of the jewels which were appraised by him and found that an excess of Rs.5.89 lakhs was 
financed due to the wrong appraisal of fineness of jevel pledged in 83 loan accounts. It is submitted that the petitioner 
has filed W.P.No.(MD). No.7658 of 20I5 before the Hon'ble Madurai Bench of Madras High Court challenging his 
disengagement and the said writ petition was dismissed by the Hon'ble court on 30.04.205. Challenging the order, he 
has filed WA. (MD). No.767 of 20I5. The said appeal was also dismissed by the Hon'ble Court. It is only thereafter, 
the petitioner has raised the present industrial dispute before the Labour Commissioner. It is submitted that the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court vide its order dated l0.03.2006 in Civil Appeal No.7986 of 2004 has clearly stated that there 
is no employer and employee relationship between the Bank and jewel appraiser like the petitioner. It is submitted 
that the petitioner was engaged by the branch as Business Correspondent through an agreement and later was 
empanelled as jewel appraiser by the Sevalpati branch. The petitioner was paid commission as per the agreement. The 
averment that the petitioner discharged his duties without any room for complaints is denied as there were complaints 
against him by the customers of the Bank. Based on the complaints, the Bank conducted re-appraisals of the jewels 
appraised by the petitioner and ascertained that an excess of Rs.5.89 lakh was financed due to his wrong appraisal. 
The petitioner was dis-empanelled as jewel appraiser based on the complaints and re-appraisals was done by the 
Bank. The petitioner is not an employee of the Bank. The Bank is only using his technical service as appraiser of 
jewels for the purpose of granting jewel loans. His remuneration is purely based on the commission which is paid by 
the customers. Further the petitioner is free to carry out any job after the assessment is over. In fact petitioner is also 
running a chit fund business even while he was engaged as Jewel Appraiser/Business Correspondent. It is submitted

that the petitioner is not an employee of the Bank. His services were utilized by the Bank for appraisal of jewels and

6. Heard the learned counsels appearing on behalf of the either side and perused the records. The point that 
arises for my determination is whether the Jewel Appraiser in the Respondent Bank is workman u/s.2(S) of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947. 


7. As per definition of section 2(s) of the Industrial Disputes Act, !947, workman is a person employed to do 
manual, technical, unskilled, skilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory work subject to wage limit. The 
question is what is the nature of work of the Jewel Appraiser. It is admitted by the Petitioner that his main work is to 
examine the purity of gold and take commission from the person who pledge the jewel in the Respondent bank and 
take the loan amount. The Respondent also stated that the bank did not pay remuneration to the Petitioner and he 
gets commission from the person who pledge the jewel in the bank. Thus, this fact is established that the Petitioner 
is taking commission per transaction from the customer, who pledge the jewel in the bank and the Petitioner is not 
under the control of the bank, he is free to work in multiple banks and there is no relationship of employer and 
employee with the Respondent bank and the Petitioner. Further, as relied on by the Respondent, the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court the case of the General Manager, Indian Overseas Bank Vs. Workmen reported in (2006) 3 SCC 
729 has categorically held that Jewel Appraisers are not workmen under the provisions of the Act. Therefore, since 
the Petitioner/Jewel Appraiser is not a workman, he is not entitled to get any relief under the Act. The reference is 
answered accordingly. 


AWARD 


In light of the above discussion, as the Petitioner is not a workman and no employer-employee relationship exists 
between the Respondent /bank and the Petitioner, he is not entitled to get any relief and thus, the industrial dispute is 
dismissed accordingly.

2. The Petitioner claimed that he was employed as sub-staff by the 2" Party/Respondent bank continuously 
from 0l--2002 till 3l-03-2009 and was paid Rs.!50/- per day through voucher and the same can be verified from

Petitioner from 3!-03-2009 is against the provisions of Industrial Dispute Act and the principles of Natural Justice. 
Since the Petitioner has worked as sub staff for more than 6 years with continuity of service, the 2" 
Party/Respondent should have regularized his service. Though the Petitioner requested the Respondent Bank on

Therefore, the Petitioner filed a petition in R.C.No.7/22/20I5, U/S 2(A) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947, before

The refusal of employment to the Petitioner from 3l-03-2009 by the 2 Party Respondent without any notice and

3. It is submitted that the Petitioner was only engaged as a Coolie by the Bank and he was paid with a sum of Rs.

6. The first question that arises to decide the reference is whether the Petitioner has worked for more than 240 
days continuously as workman with the Respondent/bank. As per definition of continuous service provided under 
section 258 of the Industrial Disputes Act, !947, if a workman has worked continuously for at least 240 days 
during the 2 calendar months preceding relating to the date e.g. terminated date from the work. The Petitioner in 
the claim statement as well as oral evidence stated that he was working as a daily wager and he was paid with daily 
rate wages. He further stated that no service book was maintained for his job. On perusal of Ex.W3, which is a 
certificate issued by the Branch Manager of the Respondent bank to the Petitioner stating that Mr.Peter is working as 
sub-staff of the Gudalur branch since 0I.!.2002 purely on temporary basis and he has been paid daily wages. This 
certificate itself suggests that Petitioner had worked as daily wager and received wages for performance of his work 
every day. This certificate was issued for his good character also. Ex.W4 is copy of letter sent by Petitioner seeking 
information under RTI Act from the Respondent bank. It is not a proof of document for his service. Ex.W5 is copy 
of representation made by Petitioner to General Manager of Respondent bank against termination. Ex.W6 is copy of 
reply given by Respondent Bank to the Petitioner under RTI Act. Ex.W7 & W8 are relating to labour dispute raised

copy of proforma invoice signed by the Petitioner.

7. The Petitioner in the claim statement stated that he was employed by the Respondent bank continuously 
from 0..2002 to 3].03.2009 and was paid Rs.l50/- per day through vouchers. This statement itself suggests that 
Petitioner was working on daily wage basis. But, the Petitioner failed to furnish any documentary evidence in support 
of his claim namely attendance register, wage register etc. The Respondent bank stated that no such documents are 
available with the respondent because the Petitioner was working as coolie on daily wage basis. Although under the 
law, nature of duties determine whether the person is a workman or not. It is not important that in what manner he 
has been provided remuneration/wage, it may be daily, monthly or on contractual basis etc. Based on the above 
discussion, it may be concluded that the Petitioner has worked for more than 240 days continuously on the basis of 
daily wage. 


8. The second issue that arises for consideration is whether the Petitioner is entitled for reinstatement into 
service? 
9. The fact is established that Petitioner has worked for more than 240 days on daily wage basis. Therefore, 


he was entitled to get benefit under the provisions of section 25F of the Act, because the Respondent although stated 
that Petitioner himself stopped from coming to work and therefore, there was no need to give one month notice or 
one month pay in lieu of notice. But, the Petitioner in his affidavit clearly stated that he was stopped by oral order of 
the Respondent not to attend the work. This statement may be considered as reliable in absence of any such person’s 
evidence, who was employed in the bank branch at the time of stoppage of the Petitioner from service. 


0. The compensation may be on the following grounds:- 
a) Worked as daily wager? 

In the present case, Petitioner worked as daily wager. 

b) Long delay in raising the dispute? 


This fact is established that Petitioner has committed delay in raising the dispute. As per his statement, he worked 
up to 3l.03.2009, but raised the industrial dispute in the year 205 before the labour authorities. 


ll. As per discussion above, it is appropriate to direct the Respondent No.l to pay one month salary to the 
Petitioner and |5 days average wages to the every completed year of continuous service along with Rs.,00,000/- in 
cash as lump sum compensation within a period of three months.

०) The Respondent bank is directed to pay Rs.!,00,000/- as lump sum compensation within a period of three

5. Heard both the parties and perused the records. The points that arise for determination are - 


(i) Whether the action of the respondent /bank in terminating the services of the Petitioners after being engaged for a 
considerable period is legally justified? 


ii) Whether the claim petitions filed by the Petitioners are maintainable or not? 
(iii) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for any relief? 


6. The Petitioner has adduced oral evidence as WWI and he was cross examined by the Respondent and 
documents filed on behalf of the Petitioner were marked as Ex.W] to Wl0. Ex.WI is the copy of voucher showing 
bonus paid to the Petitioner for 20i2-l3 and 20l3-l4. Ex.W2 is copy of ledger report of the respondent bank 
account showing sundry charges paid during April, 20!3 to March, 204 for cleaning. 


6. First of all, it is worth to mention here that as per facts of the claim petitions and evidences submitted by the 
Petitioners and reply filed by the Respondent/bank, the fact is established that the Petitioners had worked with the 
Respondent/bank branches for more than 240 days continuously in one year and served from 7 to 4 years, except 
Mr. N.Karthikeyan in ID No.5/2020, who has completed two years service. All the Petitioners in their oral evidence 
in Chief and cross examination established the fact that they had worked continuously for more than 240 days. 


The relevant oral evidence in Chief/ cross examination of the Petitioner runs as under:- 
Shri N.Karthikeyan : ID No.5/2020 in his proof of affidavit/cross-examination stated as under:- 


“T joined the services of the I" Respondent on 3.72.207/2 as sub-staff at newly opened Chennimalai branch and 
worked there upto 76. /2, 20/4 and his name has been recorded against sub-staff category during zonal audit in the 
year 2073-/4. ? 


Smt.D.Poovathal : ID No.6/2020 in her proof of affidavit stated as under: - 


“T joined the service of Respondent/bank branch at Nambiyur as sweeper cum sub-staff during November, 7996 till 
46. /2. 20/4. ”. 


Shri C.Moorthi : ID No.7/2020 in his proof of affidavit stated as under:- 


“IT joined the service of the Respondent /bank branch at Perundurai on 03.08.2002 and worked till 76. /2.20/4 as 
sub-staff.” 


Smt.R.Lakshmi : ID No.8/2020 in her proof of affidavit/cross examination stated as under:- 


“I joined the service of the Respondent /bank branch at Suriyampalayam on 77.77.2007 and worked continuously till 
46./2., 20/4 as sub-staff.” 


Shri M.Ramakrishnan: ID No.9/2020 in his proof of affidavit stated as under: -

“IT joined the service of the Respondent /bank branch at Erode on 26,02./994 to 02.06. /994 as Peon and he was 
again offered job from 27.05.995 to 74.72./996 in Thindal Branch and worked from 76./2./996 to 70.79./999 in 
Perundurai branch and also from 96.97.2070 #॥॥ 76.72.20/4 in Erode branch as sub-staff.” 


7. In reply, the Respondent/Bank argued on the point that individual claim petitions filed by the Petitioners 
under the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 are not maintainable. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the 
Respondent relied on a case law in support of his contention in (957) I LLJ 27, and it was held that the dispute 
between the employer and single employee cannot be per se be an industrial dispute, but it may become the one if it is 
taken up by number of workmen. This judgement was delivered in the year 957. 


8. Section 2A of the Industrial Disputes Act, !947 was inserted in the year 4965 and came into force w.e-.f. 
0.2.965. On perusal of the inserted section, following ingredients appear to exist:- 


i) An individual workman if his service is discharged, dismissed or retrenched or otherwise terminated may 
raise an industrial dispute. 


ii) An individual workman may raise industrial dispute regarding any dispute or difference between that 
workman and his employer connected with, or arising out of, such discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination. 


iii) 

9. In the newly inserted section, the individual employee is also entitled to raise industrial dispute. Therefore, 
it cannot be said that present Petitioners are not entitled to raise industrial dispute in their personal capacity. 

0. Now, I have to decide what relief the Petitioners are entitled to? 


As per provisions of section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947, when the workman who has completed 
continuous service not less than 240 days, the workman has to be given one month 's notice in writing indicating the 
reasons for retrenchment, the wages for the period of the notice and he has to be paid retrenchment, compensation. 
The Petitioners have worked with the Respondent/Bank for more than 240 days continuously in a calendar year, if 
yes, the protection u/s.25F of the Act is available to the workmen. 


Il. Section 25F of the Act provides the following conditions before retrenchment of workmen:- 

a) One month’s notice (wages in lieu of notice) 

b) Retrenchment compensation is paid (l5 days wages of every completed year of service); & 

०) Notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government. 

2. None of these conditions were followed by the Respondent Bank. Resultantly, the retrenchment becomes 


illegal. Since, the Respondent /Bank has violated the provisions of section 25F of the Act, the workman is entitled 
for the following or more relief:- 


a) Reinstatement with back wages; 

b) Reinstatement without back wages; & 

c) Lump sum compensation instead of compensation. 

3. All the Petitioners in the above disputes have worked with the Respondent/Bank for more than five years 


except one Mr. N.Karthikeyan in ID No.5/2020, who worked for two years. As per provisions of the Industrial 
Disputes Act, 947, the workmen who has completed 240 days, is entitled for protection u/s.25F of the Act and the 
retrenchment was in violation of the provisions of the Act, the termination becomes illegal and resultantly, the 
Petitioners are entitled for reinstatement in service. 


4. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Respondent submitted that compensation is the appropriate 
relief which may be awarded in favour of the Petitioners. He relied on the judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the 
case of Mr.Ranbir Singh Vs. Life Insurance Corporation of India & Another (2023) [7 SCC 96, whereby the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court held that Respondent cannot be directed to carry out mass absorption of eleven thousand 
workers on flawed premises without following recruitment process, consistent with the principles of equality of 
opportunity governed by Article !4 & 6 of Constitution of India. The Hon’ble Court by exercising jurisdiction under 
Article 42 of the Constitution directed to fresh verification of claims of workmen and to pay compensation in lieu of 
reinstatement. He submits that the facts involved in the present case are identical to that of the case law cited above. 
It is also worth to mention here that the Hon'ble Supreme Court had invoked extraordinary power under Article 42 
of the Constitution of India. 


5. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Respondent relied on another judgement delivered by the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Jagbir Singh Vs. Haryana State Agriculture Marketing Board & Another 
(2009) 5 SCC 327. In that case, the Appellant was engaged by Respondent १०.] as a daily wager on 0.09.995 
and he was paid consolidated monthly wages of २५. ,498/-. He worked with the Respondent upto 8.07.996. The 
Hon'ble Supreme Court delivered the finding in para 3 of the order, which runs as under:- 


[भाग I—<€ve 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 2, 2026/वैशाख 2, 948 4029 


“73. In this view of the matter, we are of the opinion that as the appellant had worked only for a short period, the 
interest of justice will be subserved if the High Court's judgment is modified by directing payment of a sum of Rs 
50,000 (Rupees fifty thousand only) by way of damages to the appellant by the respondent. Such payment should be 
made within eight weeks from this date, failing which the same will h carry interest at the rate of 9% per annum." 


6. In the above cited case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that since the workmen had worked only for a 
short period, therefore, interest of justice will be sub-served, if payment of compensation of Rs.50,000/- by way of 
damages to the Appellant by the Respondent is made. 


7. In the present case in hand, except one Petitioner Shri N.Karthikeyan in ID No.5/2020, remaining four 
Petitioners had worked more than five years continuously with the Respondent /bank. But, considering equal 
protection in the eye of law to all the five Petitioners, it is appropriate to pass an order of reinstatement into service 
of the Respondent/bank. 


8. Now, I have to consider as to whether Petitioners are entitled for back wages? It is a settled law that back 
wages are not applied automatically upon setting aside termination. It depends upon surrounding facts and 
circumstances which may be described as under:- 


i) Length of service 
il) Nature of conduct: & 
ili) Gainful employment 


It is the primary duty to ascertain whether the Petitioners were gainfully employed after termination. But, there is 
material on record to show/prove that Petitioners were gainfully employed after termination. Since the Respondent / 
Bank acted arbitrarily by not giving any notice before retrenchment of workmen and failed to comply with the 
provisions of section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947, in the present case, it is appropriate to award 50% of 
back wages to workmen/workwoman in the ID Nos.6 to 9/2020 and 25% of back wages to Mr.N.Karthikeyan in ID 
No. 5/2020 along with order of reinstatement into service of Respondent/bank. 


AWARD 


9. The claim petition filed by the Petitioners are allowed. The Petitioners are entitled to the following relief:- 


i) Reinstatement of Petitioners into service within two months from the date of receipt of this Award; 

li) To grant 50% back wages to workmen in ID Nos.6 to 9/2020 and 25% of back wages to Shri N.Karthikeyan 
in ID No.5/2020. 

iii) To pay back wages to the Petitioners from the date of termination till the date of reinstatement. 


The references are answered accordingly.

AWARD 


The present reference has been made by the Central Government by its order No. L-20]/20/2023-IR(B- 
II) dated 04/05/2023 passed in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of section (l) read with sub-section 
(2A) of Section 0 of the Industrial Dispute Act 947. The terms of reference as per the schedule to the said order are 
as under: 


“Whether the demand raised by United Forum of We Banker vide letter dated 76, /2, 2027 against to the 
management of Indian Overseas bank in respect of Shri Akshay Bharat Kawade in (a) issuing penalty of 
“censure” without holding enquiry (b) causing workman loss of pay from I7.06.2020 to 70.07.2020 (c) not 
giving transfer from Ranjangaon to the nearest place from his home town is legal, proper and justifies? If 
yes, what reliefs are the Shri Akshay Bharat Kawade / union are entitled to and what other directions, if any, 
are necessary in this matter 2 


In view of the above said facts the claimant/workman has not field any statement of claim/ evidence in support of his 
case on affidavit, in spite of several opportunities given to him and taking into consideration the law as laid by the 
Hon'ble High Court in the case of V. K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court (7) and others /987 (29) FLR 94 as under: 


“Tt is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove illegality of the 
order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail. Whenever a workman 
raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative for him to file written statement 
before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is challenged and he must also produce evidence 
to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file written statement or produce evidence, the dispute referred 
by the State Government cannot be answered in favour of the workman and he would not be entitled to any relief.” 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding Officer, 
Labour Court (II), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (776) FLR 7764 Hon’ble Allahabad High Court has held as under: 


“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., V.K. Raj 
Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. 7964 (49) FLR 38 and 
Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. /996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led by or on behalf of the 
workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In such a situation it is not 
necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead evidence to establish an allegation 
made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, who would fail if no evidence is led.” 


And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 
Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2070 (726) FLR 59; wherein it has been held as 
under: 


“The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the shoulders of the 
respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead evidence first which he failed. A perusal 
of the impugned award also does not show that any evidence either oral or documentary was led by the respondent. 
In the case of no evidence, the reference has to be dismissed.” 


Mr. S.V. Alva, Learned Counsel for the Management, appeared and he prayed that the matter be dismissed for want 
of prosecution. 


[भाग [खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 2, 2026/वैशाख 2, 948 403| 
Since no statement of claim has been filed by the union in support of his case, the claim is liable to be dismissed. 
For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and the union is not entitled for any relief. 

Accordingly, the reference stands answered in terms aforesaid.

02. On receipt of the present reference, notice is issued to the second party. The second party appeared and filed 
his statement of claim. 


The case of the Second Party, in short is as under :- 


The second party has filed statement of claim at Exh. U-3. It is submitted that, the first party is nationalized 
bank. The first party having various branches all over the country. The first party having thousands of employees to 
function the work of the bank. The first party appointed second party as a Sweeper in the month of September-2008 
on daily-wages basis. It is further submitted by the second party that, the date of birth of the second party is 
30/05/988 and he belongs to Hindu-Maratha caste. His education is up to !0" Standard. He was initially appointment 
at Sonai Branch, Tq. Newasa, Ahmednagar with the first party since September-2008. He worked as a permanent 
daily- wager Sweeper / Peon. He was transferred to Jawala Branch in the year 204. His entire service record is clean 
and unblemished. It is submitted that, after appointment of the second party in the year 20l0,20Il & 20l2 the 
respondent has recruited number of vacant posts of Peon and Sweeper as per Part Time Sweeper (Hereinafter referred 
as ‘PTS’). The second party was called for interview, but he was not appointed by the first party on the permanent 
post. Thereafter, in the year 20l7 also an advertisement for the post on PTS was published and the first party has 
recruited the posts. But again the second party was not recruited on the said post. It is further submitted that, there are 
3 posts vacant out of which 06 posts are for open category on which the second party was eligible for recruitment on 
the said post.

candidates on PTS viz., Vaishali Pathare, Avinash Shirsul, Prakash Kota, Datta Myana in Ahmednagar District without 
following any legal procedure of recruitment and made them as permanent worker. It is submitted that, the candidates 
who were juniors to the second party viz., Sanket Waghmare, Kishore Shahane, Devram Hile and more than 20 other 
candidates are appointed on PTS by the first party. 


04. The second party has further submitted that, the second party has approached to the Labour Commissioner 
for the benefit of permanency and he raised dispute before the Labour Commissioner. Therefore, the first party has 
not allowed the second party to resume on his work. The first party has orally terminated the services of the second 
party w.e.f. 8/20/209. It is further submitted that, the second party has rendered continuous and unblemished 
services with the first from September-2008 till his oral termination dated |8/02/20l9. He has completed more than 
240 days of continuous service with the first party in each year. Prior to his oral termination the first party has not 
followed the due process of law and thereby violated the provisions of Sec.25-F, 25-G & 25-H of the Industrial

Definition of “retrenchment” under section 2(00) of the Industrial Disputes Act, /942 :- 


“retrenchment”’ means the termination by the employer of the service of a workman for any reason 
whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment inflicted by way of disciplinary action, but does not include : - 


(a) voluntary retirement of a workman, or 


(b) retirement of the workman on reaching the age of superannuation if the contract of employment between 
the employer and the workman concerned contains a stipulation in that behalf ; or 


(bb) termination of the service of the workman as a result of the non-renewal of the contract of employment 
between the employer and the workman concerned on its expiry or of such contract being terminated under a 
stipulation in that behalf contained therein , or 


(c) termination of the service of a workman on the ground of continued ill-health.” 


Section 2(s) “workman” means any person (including an apprentice) employed in any industry to 
do any manual, unskilled, skilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory work for hire or reward, 
whether the terms of employment be express or implied, and for the purposes of any proceeding under this 
Act in relation to an industrial dispute, includes any such person who has been dismissed, discharged or 
retrenched in connection with, or as a consequence of, that dispute, or whose dismissal, discharge or 
retrenchment has led to that dispute, but does not include any such person— 


(i) who is subject to the Air Force Act, /959 (45 of 7959), or the Army Act, /9509 (46 of 7950), or the Navy Act, 
4957 (62 of 7959) 


or (ii) who is employed in the police service or as an officer or other employee of a prison; 
or (iii) who is employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity; 


or (iv) who, being employed in a supervisory capacity, draws wages exceeding 3 [ten thousand rupees] per 
mensem or exercises, either by the nature of the duties attached to the office or by reason of the powers vested 
in him, functions mainly of a managerial nature. ]

‘25-F. _ Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen :-

Section 25-G Procedure for retrenchment.— 


Where any workman in an industrial establishment, who is a citizen of India, is to be retrenched and he

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section () and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-!20/46/208-IR(B-ID dated 27/!/20I8 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the

for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of United Bank of India in denial of promotion to Shri Sujit 
Chatterjee as Permanent Head Cashier of Bolpur Branch of United Bank of India is legal and justified or 
not? If not, what relief the workmen is entitled to?” 


| On receiving Order No. L-20/46/208-IR(B-II) dated 27/l/20l8 from the Government of India 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case No. 43 of 20l8 was registered on 
20/2/208 and notice were issued to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims.

2, Mr. Achintya Kumar Mukherjee, Vice President, Punjab National Bank Employees Organisation produced a 
copy of an application dated 26/05/2023 addressed to the Under Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, New 
Delhi stating that United Bank of India has been merged with Punjab National Bank w.e.f. 0/04/2020 as per the 
Directives of Government of India, Ministry of Finance and United Bank of India Employees Union has been 
renamed as Punjab National Bank Employees Organisation, having the same Registration Number as 4874. The case 
was adjourned on several days awaiting necessary corrigendum of Schedule by way of describing the employer bank 
as Punjab National Bank in place of United Bank of India. No such corrigendum has been received except one dated 
23/2/2024 whereby in the schedule of reference it was stated that “Union Bank of India” be read as “United Bank of 
India”. 

3: On the basis of Notice issued to the union and the employer bank, Mr. Tara Shankar Mallick, Id. Advocate 
appeared for the management of United Bank of India but did not file written statement. Mr. Achintya Kumar 
Mukherjee, then Asst. Secretary of the union represented Mr. Sujit Chatterjee, employee of the bank. Mr. Debashish 
Basu Choudhury, General Secretary of United Bank of India Employees Union initially represented the union and 
filed a claim statement on 05/02/209. Fact of the case as disclosed in the statement of claim is that United Bank of 
Inda is an industry as comprehended under section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (hereinafter referred as 
Act for the sake of brevity). Mr. Sujit Chatterjee was the senior most employee at Bolepur Branch of United Bank of 
India and was posted as Single Window Operator at the material time. On 0/05/20]4, a vacancy arose in the post of 
head cashier at Bolepur Branch of the Bank under Burdwan Regional Office due to retirement of Shri Ashish Kumar 
Das on 30/04/20I4. For the purpose of filling up the permanent vacancy in the post of Head Cashier at Bolepur 
Branch of United Bank of India, the prevailing policy is to appoint the senior most Single Window Operator of the 
branch to the post of Head Cashier. A special pay is attached to the post of Head Cashier as per the bipartite 
settlement governing the service condition of employees. It is contended that on 0I/05/204, Sujit Chatterjee being 
the senior most Single Window Operator was eligible for the post of Head Cashier as per the prevailing norms and 
policy and thereby was entitled to receive special allowance or higher pay. Case of the union is that on 05/05/204, 
Branch Manager of Bolepur Branch issued an office order for entrusting the charge of Head Cashier to the senior 
most Single Window Operator but Sujit Chatterjee by letter dated 05/05/204 declined to accept the charge of Head 
Cashier on the ground of problems in his right hand and the next seniormost workman took the charge of Head 
Cashier at Bolepur Branch in compliance with the office order issued by the Branch Manager on 05/05/204. On 
8/06/204, previous order of the Branch Manager was cancelled and fresh order was passed once again offering the 
post of Head Cashier to Sujit Chatterjee. He accepted the offer and communicated the same in writing to the authority 
on 8/06/204. Concerned workman performed his assigned job in the capacity of Head Cashier. Branch Manager on 
02/07/204 issued a letter No. BOL/STAFF/HEAD CASHIER/299/20I4-5 inviting application from Sujit Chatterjee 
regarding his willingness for the post of Head Cashier. On the same day, workman submitted application dated 
02/07/204 expressing his willingness. Contention of the union is that Regional Office of the bank at Burdwan issued 
letter dated 08/0I/20I5 addressed to the Chief Manager, DIR, Department, Head Office of the bank for selection to 
the post of Head Cashier, expressing choice of selecting Sujit Chatterjee, seniormost Single Window Operator to the 
post of Head Cashier. However, bank held up confirmation of the workman in the post of Head Cashier. Union 
stepped in and made representation before the bank authorities at different forms pressing for confirmation of Sujit 
Chatterjee to the post. Confirmation of Head Cashier was due on 23/06/20I5 with expiry of six months of probation 
period. It is contended that regional authority of the bank in an arbitrary manner and in violation of the policy of 
selection and posting of Head Cashier, removed Sujit Chatterjee from the charge of Head Cashier and handed over the 
charge of Head Cashier to a junior employee of the branch. 


4. Being dissatisfied with the illegal decision of the bank, an Industrial Dispute was raised. Conciliation 
proceeding which commenced on 25/08/20I5 at Calcutta was transferred to the office of Assistant Labour 
Commissioner (Central), Durgapur. Further case is that on 02/07/205, Regional Office of the bank transferred Sujit 
Chatterjee from Bolepur Branch to Bolepur-Bhubandanga Branch of the United Bank of India as Single Window 
Operator, the post held by him prior to his posting as Head Cashier, which is a superior post. Conciliation proceeded 
before the ALC(C), Durgapur resulted in failure and Government of India referred this Industrial Dispute for 
adjudicating the question as to whether the action of the management of United Bank of India in denying promotion 
to Sujit Chatterjee as Head Cashier of Bolepur Branch is legal and justified and whether he is entitled to any relief? 


5. In their statement of claim, union prayed for an order to the effect that denying confirmation of Sujit 
Chatterjee in the post of Head Cashier and posting a junior employee there is void and ab initio. It is further 
contended that the bank acted in an illegal manner in reverting the workman to his earlier post of Single Window 
Operator and prayed for payment of wages attached to the post of Head Cashier with consequential benefits from the 
date of taking the charge of workman under the order of the Competent Authority. 


6. It is an admitted fact that during pendency of the Industrial Dispute before the Tribunal, by virtue of the 
Extraordinary Gazette Notification of India dated 04/03/2020, Ministry of Finance issued a Notification bearing 
G.S.R. 53(E) whereby there was amalgamation of Punjab National Bank with Oriental Bank of Commerce and 
United Bank of India under Punjab National Bank Scheme, 2020 and it came into force on 0/04/2020. After such 
amalgamation there has been no corrigendum of Schedule incorporating Punjab National Bank as the employer 
company, therefore reference case was considered only after issuance of Notice to the United Bank of India. In course 
of time, United Bank of India preferred not to participate before the Tribunal.

7. To reach a logical consequence in respect of the Industrial Dispute, the case was fixed up for ex-parte 
hearing. Mr. Achintya Kumar Mukherjee, sole witness in this case appeared in the capacity of the union 
representative of United Bank of India Employees Union, now known as Punjab National Bank Employees 
Organisation. In course of evidence, he reiterated the case of the union disclosed in the claim statement. Witness in 
support of the case produced the following documents: 


(i) Copy of circular No. PD(DIR)/DIR//7/OM-042/0- dated 7/06/200 is marked as Exhibit W-]. 


(il) Copy of letter dated 08/0/20I5 issued by the Chief Manager informing that Sujit Chatterjee, seniormost 
staff member (Single Window Operator) was selected to function as Head Cashier before permanent Head Cashier for 
Bolepur Branch was selected is marked as Exhibit W-2. 


(iil) Copy of Gazette Notification of Ministry of Finance dated 04/03/2020 by which there has been merger of 
Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India with Punjab National Bank, is collectively marked as 
Exhibit W-3. 


(iv) Copy of letter issued by Sujit Chatterjee on 8/06/204 addressed to the Chief Manager, United Bank of 
India, Bolepur Branch stating that he was ready to accept the charge of permanent head cashier of the branch is 
marked as Exhibit W-4. 


(५) Copy of office order No. 30/20I4 dated 8/06/20I4 by which the Chief Manager of United Bank of India, 
Bolepur Branch requested Sujit Chatterjee to take over charge of Head Cashier of the branch on the basis of seniority 
is marked as Exhibit W-5. 


(५) Copy of office order dated 02/07/20I4 by which Sujit Chatterjee was put incharge of Head Cashier of 
United Bank of India, Bolepur Branch is marked as Exhibit W-6. 


(शा) Copy of office order dated by which Sujit Chatterjee remained incharge till 0/2/20l4 and handed over 
keys to Baloi Mal, next senior person is marked as Exhibit W-6/]. 


(vii) | Copy of order dated 27/0/205 by which Baloi Mal, next seniormost was advised to take charge of cash 
department is marked as Exhibit W-6/2. 


(ix) Copy of order dated 28/03/205 by which Rubi Chatterjee was advised to take charge of cash department 
from Sujit Chatterjee is marked as Exhibit W-6/3. 


(x) Copy of order dated 28/04/20I5 by which Rubi Chakraborty was advised to take charge of Head Cashier 
from Sujit Chatterjee until further order, is marked as Exhibit W-6/4. 


(xi) Copy of letter dated 02/07/20l4 issued by the Chief Manager seeking willingness of the candidate for 
appointment to the post of Head Cashier, is marked as Exhibit W-7. 


(xii) Copy of letter issued by Sujit Chatterjee dated 02/07/20I4 addressed to the Chief Manager, United Bank of 
India, Bolepur Branch expressing his willingness to accept the post, is marked as Exhibit W-8. 


(xiii) | Copy of transfer order dated 02/07/20I5 whereby Sujit Chatterjee along with five others were transferred to 
other branches of United Bank of India is marked as Exhibit W-9. 


(xiv) | Copy of order dated 03/07/205 issued by Senior Manager (Admn.) of United Bank of India, Burdwan 
Region appointing Ruby Chakraborty as Head Cashier at Bolepur Branch of United Bank of India is marked as 
Exhibit W-l0.None appeared to cross-examine the Witness and he was discharged. 


8. Mr. Achintya Kumar Mukherjee, union representative submitted that by order No. 30/l4 dated 8/06/204, 
Chief Manager, United Bank of India, Bolepur Branch requested Sujit Chatterjee to take the charge of Head Cashier 
of the Bolepur branch on the basis of seniority (copy of order is produced as Exhibit W-5). On 02/07/204, Sujit 
Chatterjee expressed his willingness to take the charge (Exhibit W-8) in response to letter dated 02/07/204, inviting 
his willingness to the post. Mr. Achintya Kumar Mukherjee submitted that subsequently, one Baloi Mal, next 
seniormost was advised to take the charge of Head Cashier, thereafter on 28/04/20l5 one Ruby Chakraborty was 
advised to take the charge of Head Cashier from Sujit Chatterjee until further order. Mr. Mukherjee argued that 
instead of selecting Sujit Chatterjee, the seniormost Single Window Operator to the post of Head Cashier, 
Management in an illegal manner transferred him to Bolepur-Bhubandanga Branch by order dated 02/07/20I5 
(Exhibit W-9). Union representative strenuously argued that the union has raised this Industrial Dispute only to 
consolidate its moral right against arbitrary action of the bank and not for any material gain or financial benefits. 
Concluding his argument, Mr. Mukherjee asserted that it would be a moral victory for the union of the bank if this 
Tribunal finds that management illegally deprived Sujit Chatterjee from his legitimate dues of being promoted to the 
post of Head Cashier of the bank instead of appointing junior members. 


9. I have considered the materials in the case record, evidence adduced by the union witness (WW-I) and 
argument advanced on behalf of the employee’s union of United Bank of India. At the outset it is worthwhile to note 
that there has been a fundamental transformation in the constitution of the employer bank on account of its 


4052 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 2, 2026/VAISAKHA 2, 946 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


amalgamation with Oriental Bank of Commerce and Punjab National Bank w.e.f. 0I/04/2020. Since United Bank of 
India is a component of amalgamation, finality of this adjudication will bind respective parties at the level of their 
present disposition. 


0. Crux of issue for adjudication in this reference is whether the management of the bank acted in a legal and 
justified manner by denying the post of permanent Head Cashier to Sujit Chatterjee at Bolepur Branch of the United 
Bank of India. In the instant case, Sujit Chatterjee has not been examined as witness despite the fact that Mr. Debashis 
Basu Chaudhury, General Secretary of the union on 05/02/209 named Sujit Chatterjee in the list of witness. It is 
therefore, unknown as to whether the person concerned had any personal grievance for not being selected to the post 
of Head Cashier of Bolepur Branch. Union has come up with a plea that Sujit Chatterjee being the seniormost Single 
Window Operator was entitled to the post of Head Cashier at the bank on retirement of Ashish Kumar Das on 
30/04/204. In course of argument, it is submitted by the union representative that the post of Head Cashier is not a 
promotional post but a special pay is attached to such post which is usually given to the seniormost employee as per 
bipartite settlement. It transpires from pleading of the union that by office order No. 33/204 dated 02/07/20I4 
(Exhibit W-6), Sujit Chatterjee was again advised to take the charge of Head Cashier of the branch until further order. 
Arrangements were made by the Branch Manager from time to time deputing various persons to function as Head 
Cashier (In-charge) during leave of Sujit Chatterjee. There was no appointment to the post of Head Cashier on 
permanent basis until 03/07/20I5. From the testimony of WW-I it is gathered that by order dated 02/07/205, Sujit 
Chatterjee along with five others were transferred to other branches of United Bank of India and copy of order is 
produced as Exhibit W-9. Without objection against order of transfer at any point of time, Sujit Chatterjee joined the 
post of Single Window Operator at Bolepur-Bhubandanga Branch of United Bank of India on 03/07/20I5. A judicial 
Notice can be taken of the fact that employment in Banking job is transferrable in nature. Mr. Achintya Kumar 
Mukherjee, union representative fairly submitted that Sujit Chatterjee had completed five years of his posting at 
Bolepur Branch of United Bank of India and his transfer was due. Decision of the management of transferring Sujit 
Chatterjee to Bolepur-Bhubandanga Branch of the bank by order dated 02/07/20]4 therefore, does not suffer from any 
illegality. Once the concerned employee has been transferred to another branch of the bank, he has no locus standi to 
claim any post in his earlier place of work by dint of his seniority in that branch. Exhibit W-l0 is a copy of order 
dated 03/07/20I5 whereby Senior Manager (Admn.) of United Bank of India appointed Smt. Ruby Chakraborty as 
Head Cashier of the Bolepur Branch of United Bank of India. The union has no right to dispute the administrative 
decision taken on 03/07/205 for filling up the post of Head Cashier after transfer of the seniormost staff concerned. 


ll. Under the facts and circumstances discussed above, I have no hesitation to hold that management of United 
Bank of India committed no illegality by appointing Smt. Ruby Chakraborty as Head Cashier of Bolepur Branch on 
03/07/205 and there was no breach of any moral principle in not considering Sujit Chatterjee for the said post when 
he joined his new place of posting. Such decision on part of the management doesn’t amount to deprivation of a 
senior employees to any promotional post which has fallen vacant. Consequently, I hold that there is no merit in the 
Industrial Dispute and the same is dismissed. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed ex-parte against the union of the bank. Concerned union is not entitled to any 
relief in this case. Let an Award be drawn up in the light of my above discussion. Let copies of Award be

दिनांक 27.03.2002 को छपरा जेल के सभी कैदियों ने संजय राय, वकील राय, शशि भूषण सिंह और जटा शंकर सिंह की अगुवाई में 
अपने साथियों के साथ, गृह विभाग, बिहार के छपरा जेल से भागलपुर तथा बक्सर की जिलों में उनके स्थानांतरण के आदेश से उग्र होकर, जेल के 
कर्मचारियों, पुलिस कार्मिकों और मजिस्ट्रेटों के साथ झड़प शुरू कर दी, जिन्हें स्थानांतरण के उपरोक्त आदेश को निष्पादित करने के लिए नियुक्त 
किया गया था। उन्होंने अपने वार्डो के गेटों को क्षतिग्रस्त कर दिया तथा जेल परिसर में सरकारी संपत्ति को नुकसान पहुंचाया। उनके हिंसक कृत्यों 
ने जेल के नियमित कामकाज को बुरी तरह बाधित किया तथा जेल के अन्य कैदियों और जेल कार्मिकों के बीच अव्यवस्था, दहशत और आतंक पैदा 
कर दिया। पुलिस, मजिस्ट्रेट और जेल अधिकारियों द्वारा उन्हें शांत करने के सभी प्रयास व्यर्थ गए। सरकारी कार्मिकों के साथ दुर्व्यवहार किया 
गया और उन्हें जबरन जेल परिसर से बाहर निकाल दिया गया। इन आक्रामक कैदियों ने जेल पर पूरी तरह से नियंत्रण कर लिया। दिनांक 
29.03.2002 तक यह स्थिति बनी रही। इन दो दिनों के दौरान, विद्रोही कैदियों ने बाहर से हथियार और विस्फोटक/बम एकत्र कर लिए क्योंकि 
उनका जेल परिसर पर पूर्ण नियंत्रण था और जेल परिसर के चारों ओर की सड़क एक सामान्य रास्ता थी जहां से उनके साथी उपरोक्त सामान को 
परिसर में फेंकने में कामयाब रहे। यह उल्लेखनीय है कि उस समय छपरा मंडल जेल के अंदर लगभग 1200 कैदी थे। 


दिनांक 30.03.2002 को स्थिति और बिगड़ गई तथा स्थिति को संभालने के लिए, कुंदन Foor, पुलिस अधीक्षक सारण के नेतृत्व में 
पुलिस कार्मिकों को तैनात किया गया और जेल परिसर को दंगाई कैदियों से प्रशासनिक नियंत्रण में वापस लाने के लिए कार्रवाई शुरू की गई। 
बार-बार चेतावनी देने के बावजूद, दंगाई कैदियों ने पुलिस दल पर पत्थर फेंकना जारी रखा। स्थिति की गंभीरता को देखते हुए तथा अन्य कोई 
विकल्प न होने के कारण, कुंदन HO, पुलिस अधीक्षक सारण ने अर्जुन लाल, पुलिस उप-निरीक्षक और सिपाही जितेंद्र सिंह के साथ जेल की 
दीवार पर चढ़ने का निर्णय लिया। आक्रामक कैदियों द्वारा फेंके जा रहे पत्थरों का सामना करते हुए ये पुलिस कार्मिक जेल की दीवार पर चढ़ने में 
सफल रहे और उन्होंने दीवार से सटे जेल के प्रशासनिक भवन की छत पर पोजीशन ले ली। इस स्थान से, पत्थरबाजी करने वाले कैदियों से वापस 
अपने वार्ड में जाने और जेल के बाहरी परिसर को खाली करने की अपील की गई। हालांकि, कैदी और अधिक हिंसक हो गए और उन्होंने पत्थर 
तथा बम फेंकना शुरू कर दिया, कुछ गोलीबारी भी शुरू हो गई जिससे पुलिस दल बाल-बाल बचा। इस घटना में पुलिस अधीक्षक सारण के पैर 
और हाथ में मामूली चोटें आईं। चोटों के बावजूद, पुलिस अधीक्षक सारण ने उप-निरीक्षक अर्जुन लाल के साथ अपने सहयोगियों का नेतृत्व किया 
और अपनी पोजीशन पर अडिग रहे। सशस्त्र कैदियों ने दी जा रही चेतावनियों को अनसुना करते हुए अपने हिंसक कृत्यों को जारी रखा। उन्होंने 
गैस सिलेंडरों का इस्तेमाल करके, जिन्हें वे जेल के गेट पर लाए थे, से जेल के मुख्य गेट को उड़ाने की धमकी भी दी। उन्होंने पुलिस बैरकों से सटी 
जेल की पश्चिमी दीवार को तोड़ना शुरू कर दिया। उनके इरादे को भांपते हुए, पुलिस अधीक्षक सारण ने पुलिस कार्मिकों को हिंसक कैदियों को 
वापस अपनी बैरकों में लौटने के लिए मजबूर करने के लिए प्रभावी गोलीबारी शुरू करने का निदेश दिया। इस प्रकार दंगाई कैदियों को अपनी 
बैरकों में वापस जाने के लिए मजबूर किया गया। इसके बाद पुलिस अधीक्षक सारण अपने साथ आए कुछ पुलिस कार्मिकों के साथ प्रशासनिक

मोहम्मद रफ़ीक़, एस.जी.सीटी इशतियाक अहमद खान और सिपाही सफ़ीर लोन ने प्रथम घेराबंदी में बहादुरी से लड़ते हुए दो खूंखार आतंकवादियों

ले ली और वे अपराधियों का इंतजार करने लगे। सुबह लगभग 05:00 बजे, प्रयागराज की तरफ से नीली अपाचे मोटरसाइकिल पर दो लोग आते

बार-बार चुनौती दी गई, लेकिन उनकी चेतावनी बेकार गई। भागने की कोशिश में अपराधियों ने मोटरसाइकिल को अचानक मोड़ लिया और वे

मुड़ गए, लेकिन मोटरसाइकिल अनियंत्रित होकर गिर गई। रोकने की कोशिश करने पर, पीठ पर बैग लटकाए व्यक्ति ने अपनी कमर में खोंसी 
पिस्तौल निकाली और पुलिस पर गोलियां चला दीं, जिससे उप-निरीक्षक अतुल चतुर्वेदी, उप-निरीक्षक प्रदीप कुमार सिंह और हेड कांस्टेबल

Kundan Krishnan, IPS Superintendent of Police GM 

2; Arjun Lal Sub-Inspector GM 

3. Jitendra Singh Constable GM 


Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


On 27.03.2002 led by Sanjay Rai, Vakil Rai, Shashi Bhushan Singh and Jata Shanker Singh, all inmates of Chapra 
jail along with their supporters, infuriated by the orders of the Home Department, Bihar for their transfer from Chapra jail to 
Bhagalpur and Buxar jails, started scuffles with the jail employees, police personnel and magistrates, deputed to execute the 
above order of transfer. They damaged the gates of their wards and destroyed government property in the jail compound. Their 
violent actions badly disturbed the routine functioning of the jail and created disorder, panic and terror among other jail inmates 
and jail personnel. All the efforts made by the police, magistrates and jail authorities to pacify them went in vain. The 
government personnel were abused and forcibly driven out of the jail premises. These aggressive prisoners took complete 
control of the jail in their hands. This situation prevailed till 29.3.2002. During these two days, the mutinous prisoners had 
collected arms and explosives/ bombs from outside as they had total control of the jail campus and the road around the jail 
compound was a general thoroughfare from where their supporters managed to throw into the compound the above items. It 
may be mentioned that at this time there were approximately 1200 prisoners inside the Chapra Divisional Jail. 


On 30.03.2002, the situation worsened in order to salvage the situation, under the leadership of Kundan Krishnan, SP 
Saran who deployed police personnel, action was started to bring the jail campus back under administrative control from the 
rioting prisoners. Despite repeated warning, the rioting prisoners continued to use stones against the police party. Considering 
the gravity of situation and having no alternative, Kundan Krishnan, SP Saran with Arjun Lal, Sub Inspector of Police and 
Constable Jitendra Singh took the decision to climb the jail wall. Led by the SP, these police personnel facing a mob of stone 
being thrown by aggressive prisoners managed to scale the jail wall and get a foothold on the roof of the administrative building 
of the jail adjoining the wall. From this location, an appeal was made to the stone pelting prisoners to go back into their wards 
and vacate the outer campus of the jail. However, the prisoners grew more violent and they began to throw stones and bombs, 
some firing was also started from which the police party escaped narrowly. The SP Saran got minor injuries on his legs and 
hand during this incident. Despite injuries the, SP Saran along with SI Arjun Lal led their subordinates and stood their position 
undeterred. The armed prisoners, turning a deaf ear to the warnings being given, continued their violent acts. They even 
threatened to blow up the main gate of the jail using gas cylinders which they had brought to the jail gate. They proceeded to 
break the western wall of the jail adjoining the police barracks. Sensing their intention, the SP Saran directed the police 
personnel to start effective firings in order to force the violent prisoners to retreat back into their barracks. The rioting prisoners 
were thus forced to withdraw to their barracks. The SP Saran then entered the jail compound by climbing down from the roof 
of the administrative building along with the few police personnel who were accompanying him. Then they removed the gas 
cylinders from the jail gate thus allowing for the use of welding machines to cut open the jammed main gate of the jail. As the 
Police parties entered into the jail premises, the armed prisoners positioned in the jail compound, began to throw stones and 
discharged a volley of fire on the entering police personnel. For some time, the entire jail compound was turned into a battle 
field. The defiant prisoners having no respect for the police and the administration were in no mood to surrender and acted like 
a gang of hardened criminals. Finding no alternative, the police personnel under the leadership of SP Saran started retaliatory 
firings. This situation continued for half an hour. Eventually, the retaliatory action by the police forced the aggressive prisoners 
to stop firing and surrender. At about 14.30 hours, during a search made by the magistrates deputed with the police, the bodies 
of 4(four) prisoners were found along with arms and live cartridges. Another 7(seven) prisoners were found injured and were 
removed to hospital where another two prisoners later succumbed to their injuries. The gravity of the situation can be judged 
from the fact that a total of 48 tear gas shells, three tear gas hand grenades and 234 rounds were fired by the police during the 
above action. 


The leadership displayed by Kundan Krishnan, SP Saran and SI Arjun Lal, during this violent episode which 
continued for 3-4 hours, highlights their commitment to the call of duty and their act of bravery in a most adverse situation. SP 
Saran along with his subordinates, facing the maximum risk of life, displayed qualitative leadership from the front. Both the 
above officers by dint of their indomitable courage and determination, prevented a violent jailbreak by over a thousand 
prisoners. 


In this operation, S/Shri Kundan Krishnan, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Arjun Lal, Sub-Inspector and Jitendra Singh, 
Constable of Bihar Police displayed conspicuous gallantry, courage and devotion to duty of a higher order.
